life_summary: Marion G. Romney was born September 19, 1897, in Colonia Juárez, Chihuahua, Mexico, to LDS pioneer settlers. His parents were among the Latter-day Saint colonists in Mexico, giving him an international and cross-cultural perspective unusual for his generation. Romney developed a deep commitment to agricultural development and community building, reflecting his pioneering heritage. He married Ida Jensen on September 12, 1924, in the Salt Lake Temple, and the couple had two biological sons, one of whom died in infancy, and one adopted child. Romney spent significant portions of his professional life focused on church welfare principles and Book of Mormon scholarship, emerging as a thought leader in both areas.
church_summary: Romney served as a missionary in Australia from 1920 to 1923, gaining experience in international church work. He was called as an Assistant to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 1941 and became a member of the Quorum of the Twelve in 1951. From 1961 to 1972, he served as an area supervisor for Mexico, helping to strengthen the church's work in the land of his birth. He was appointed Second Counselor in the First Presidency in 1972, serving until 1982, when he became First Counselor until 1985. He concluded his service as Quorum President from 1985 until his death in 1988. Romney was renowned as a pioneer of church welfare initiatives and a careful student of Book of Mormon teachings.
burial_place: Wasatch Lawn Memorial Park, Salt Lake City, Utah
teaching_emphasis: Book of Mormon scholarship and doctrine
